# PhoneAsController

> Free Windows app that turns an Android phone into an Xbox 360 or DualShock 4 controller, racing wheel, keyboard and trackpad. It works with no internet and no router, using the laptop's own Wi-Fi hotspot or a USB cable. Nothing is installed on the phone.

## Key facts

- PC: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. Download is a 48 MB zip; 113 MB once installed.
- Phone: Android with Chrome. Built and tested mainly on a Samsung Galaxy S22 Ultra. iPhones have not been tested.
- Connection: the laptop's password-protected Wi-Fi hotspot (default), USB tethering, or a shared Wi-Fi network.
- Aeroplane mode: the hotspot needs the laptop's Wi-Fi on, which Windows allows during aeroplane mode.
- Controllers: Windows sees a standard Xbox 360 or DualShock 4 controller through the ViGEmBus driver. Some anti-cheat systems may block virtual controllers.
- Players: up to 8 phones. Many Windows games read at most 4 Xbox controllers.
- Closing the window stops everything within a few seconds, with nothing left running in the background or at startup.
- Limits: Install.exe isn't commercially code-signed, so Windows shows a warning on first run. Tilt steering and motion need a secure page that shows a certificate warning.
